content: LRRC57, also referred to as Leucine Rich Repeat Containing 57, is a protein encoded by the LRRC57 gene in humans. Function The precise biological function of LRRC57 remains unknown. However, it belongs to the leucine-rich repeat (LRR) family of proteins, which are recognized for their involvement in protein-protein interactions. Protein Sequence As is typical for leucine-rich repeat proteins, the amino acid sequence of LRRC57 is organized in a manner that highlights the repeating units. Each repeat begins with a β-strand, which contributes to the formation of a β-sheet on the concave side of the protein. The convex side of the protein is formed by the latter portion of each repeat, which can adopt various structural conformations, including α-helices, 3₁₀ helices, β-turns, and occasionally short β-strands. The sequence layout facilitates the identification of the LxxLxLxxNxL consensus sequence characteristic of LRRs. Homology LRRC57 is highly conserved across species, as demonstrated by multiple sequence alignments generated using Clustal X2. Regions of high conservation and the repeating units are highlighted in cyan and yellow, respectively. Orthologs of the human LRRC57 protein have been identified in various species, though not all orthologs are included in the alignment. These orthologs were identified through BLAT and BLAST searches. Gene Neighborhood The LRRC57 gene exhibits notable relationships with its neighboring genes. In humans, it is located upstream of the HAUS2 gene and downstream of the SNAP23 gene. This arrangement is conserved in the mouse ortholog, as well as in most vertebrates. The close proximity between LRRC57 and HAUS2/CEP27 (alternative names for the same gene) is particularly interesting. In humans, the exons of these genes are separated by 50 base pairs, whereas in mice, they overlap. This close genomic relationship may contribute to the high conservation of LRRC57, as mutations would need to be stable in both genes simultaneously. Additionally, the relationship with the downstream neighbor SNAP23 is intriguing. According to the AceView database, 373 base pairs of this gene are antisense to spliced gene SNAP23, raising the possibility of regulated alternate expression. Aligning the reverse complement of the LRRC57 cDNA with the SNAP23 cDNA reveals significant similarity, as shown in partial alignments. Predicted Post-Translational Modifications Using tools from the ExPASy Proteomics site, several post-translational modifications have been predicted for LRRC57 in Homo sapiens. Predicted phosphorylation sites are highlighted in cyan, while other modifications are labeled in yellow. Conserved predictions across all four analyzed organisms are marked with red boxes. Notably, phosphorylation at S201 and sulfation at Y224 are the only well-conserved modifications across all four species. Structure The three-dimensional structure of LRRC57 has not yet been determined. However, a protein BLAST search against the Protein Data Bank (PDB) identified a similar protein (PDB: 2O6Q) with an E-value of 3E−14. This protein, described as Eptatretus burgeri (inshore hagfish) variable lymphocyte receptor A29, also contains leucine-rich repeats, with seven repeats of the same length as those in LRRC57.
